page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c2m1.large is an entry-tier virtual server from the shared t6 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. Hardware architecture is based on the x86_64 platform, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is allocated 2 burstable vCPUs configured across 1 physical core with 2 threads. System memory totals 1.0 GB, which provides 0.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server does not bundle local disk storage, requiring remote block volumes for persistent data, and features no GPU acceleration or provisioned baseline network bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in lower performance brackets, consistent with its shared and burstable resource configuration. Under stress-ng, it achieved a single-core score of 1301.59 and a multi-core score of 2581.56, placing it in the bottom quartile of tested systems. PassMark CPU testing yielded an overall score of 1116.23, with extended instructions reaching 800.10 and encryption scoring 342.74. While small-block cached read bandwidth reached 185.29 GB/sec, large uncached 256 MB block memory reads dropped to 0.1 GB/sec. Application testing delivered 1.0 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 2.67 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is centered on providing minimal resource footprints for non-continuous, budget-conscious deployments. The primary tradeoff is the strict 1.0 GB RAM ceiling and shared burstable CPU model, which make the instance susceptible to memory exhaustion and CPU throttling during sustained loads. Consequently, the server is suitable for lightweight background utilities, simple automation tasks, microservices with low memory overhead, and basic staging or test environments.
